name: Russia
sources: Labour Code of the Russian Federation (197-FZ)

rules.match_hint: employer, HR or agent keeps, holds or stores the worker's passport, patent or other documents
rules.why: Taking a passport as a pledge or guarantee is an offence. Your employer has no legal reason to keep your passport or work patent, and you need them with you for police checks.
rules.law_text: Code of Administrative Offences, Art. 19.17(2): "Taking an identity document (passport) as a pledge is punishable by a warning or an administrative fine of one hundred roubles." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Keep your passport and patent yourself. If they were taken, complain to the labour inspectorate (онлайнинспекция.рф) or the police (112).

rules.match_hint: more than 40 hours a week of normal working time, e.g. 6 days x 12 hours = 72 hours
rules.why: Normal working time cannot be more than 40 hours a week. Anything above that is overtime, which needs your written consent and is limited to 4 hours a day and 120 hours a year.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 91: "Normal working time may not exceed 40 hours a week." Art. 99: overtime needs the worker's written consent and "must not exceed 4 hours a day and 120 hours a year for each worker." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Ask for a schedule within 40 hours. Write down the hours you actually work every day.

rules.match_hint: overtime unpaid, 'included in salary', paid at normal rate, or hours worked above hours paid
rules.why: Overtime must be paid at least 1.5 times for the first 2 hours and at least double after that.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 152: overtime is paid "for the first two hours of work at no less than one and a half times the rate, and for the following hours at no less than double the rate." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Compare hours worked with hours paid on your payslip. Keep your own record and complain if they don't match.

rules.match_hint: deductions for housing, dormitory, food, uniform, workwear, or any deduction above 20% of the wage
rules.why: The employer can only deduct in a few cases listed by law (like unearned advances or counting errors). Housing, food or uniforms can only be paid from your wage if you asked for it in writing. All deductions together cannot exceed 20% of each payment.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 137: "Deductions from a worker's wages are made only in the cases provided for by this Code and other federal laws." Art. 138: "The total of all deductions at each wage payment may not exceed 20 percent" (50% in cases set by federal law). (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Do not sign a request for deductions you don't want. Check each payslip against the 20% limit.

rules.match_hint: fine (штраф) for lateness, mistakes or rule-breaking deducted from wages
rules.why: Employers cannot fine workers. The only disciplinary penalties allowed are a reprimand, a warning or dismissal.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 192: "Disciplinary penalties not provided for by federal laws, charters and regulations on discipline are not allowed." The Code's penalties are a reprimand, a warning and dismissal; fines are not among them. (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Ask for the fine to be returned. Complain to the labour inspectorate if it isn't.

rules.match_hint: worker must pay a fine, penalty or several months' salary for resigning or leaving early
rules.why: You can resign at any time by giving 2 weeks' written notice. A worker only has to pay for direct actual damage they caused, so a fixed penalty for quitting is not allowed.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 80: "The worker has the right to terminate the employment contract by warning the employer in writing at least two weeks in advance." Art. 238: "The worker must compensate the employer for direct actual damage caused." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Don't sign this clause. If you want to leave, give written notice 2 weeks ahead and keep a copy.

rules.match_hint: salary paid once a month, or later than 15 days after the period
rules.why: Wages must be paid at least every half month, and no later than 15 days after the period they cover.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 136: "Wages are paid at least every half month," no later than "15 calendar days from the end of the period for which they were accrued." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Ask for pay twice a month as the law requires.

rules.match_hint: no payslip, or deductions without a reason
rules.why: Every time you are paid, the employer must tell you in writing what your pay is made of and the amount and reason for every deduction.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 136: when paying wages the employer must inform each worker in writing "of the components of the wage [...] of the amounts and grounds of the deductions made [...] of the total amount to be paid." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Ask for a written payslip (расчётный листок) every pay day.

rules.match_hint: work 7 days a week, no day off
rules.why: Every worker must get weekly days off.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 111: "All workers are granted days off (uninterrupted weekly rest)." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Ask for fixed days off in the contract.

rules.match_hint: less than 28 calendar days annual leave, or no leave
rules.why: You get at least 28 calendar days of paid leave a year.
rules.law_text: Labour Code Art. 115: "The annual basic paid leave is granted to workers for 28 calendar days." (our translation from Russian)
rules.action: Ask for the leave clause to match the law.
